about: Push It Somewhere Else Patrick is a two-panel shot of Patrick Star in front of a worried crowd of Bikini Bottom citizens. In the top panel he stretches his arms out to the side, and in the bottom panel he pushes both hands the other way, miming the act of moving a whole problem somewhere else. His eager, slightly crazed face suggests he thinks this is brilliant. The meme uses the gesture to propose a lazy, short-sighted fix that technically solves nothing, only relocates it.
origin: The frames are from the 2001 SpongeBob episode "Sandy, SpongeBob, and the Worm". When a giant worm threatens the town, Patrick suggests taking Bikini Bottom and pushing it somewhere else.
usage:
The top box starts the proposal, classically "why don't we take X". The bottom box finishes it, "and push it somewhere else" or "and put it Y". Reading across the two panels completes Patrick's plan.

The best captions describe a fix that only shifts the problem: moving clutter into a closet, renaming a bug a feature, transferring debt to a new card. Keep the grammar of the original line so readers hear Patrick's voice, then make the destination the punchline.
ideas: why don't we take all the dirty dishes
and put them in the oven
why don't we take the bug
why don't we take this meeting
why don't we take our problems
and push them to next sprint
why don't we take all the clothes on the chair
and move them to the other chair
why don't we take the whole team
and put it in a group chat
